database_summary: Small airline/airport/flights data model. Three tables: airlines (lookup of carriers), airports (lookup of airports by code), and flights (each flight defined by airline id, flight number, source and destination airport codes). Flights references airports; flights.Airline references airlines.uid. The data appears to be a static reference dataset (no timestamps).

accepted.name: airlines_dim
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  uid,
  Airline,
  Abbreviation,
  Country
FROM
  airlines
accepted.description: Normalized airline dimension: one row per airline carrier with stable descriptive attributes. Use to join airline names/abbreviations/country onto facts or to filter/select carriers. | Use for: List carriers with their abbreviations and country; Filter carriers by Country; Join airline descriptive attributes to flights

accepted.name: airports_dim
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  AirportCode,
  AirportName,
  City,
  Country,
  CountryAbbrev
FROM
  airports
accepted.description: Normalized airport dimension: one row per airport (AirportCode) exposing city, name and country fields. Useful for joining to flights or filtering by country/city. | Use for: Look up airport details by AirportCode; Filter airports by Country or City; Join airport descriptive attributes to flights

accepted.name: flights_dim
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Airline,
  FlightNo,
  SourceAirport,
  DestAirport
FROM
  flights
accepted.description: Canonical flight definitions (fact rows) exposing carrier id, flight number, source and destination airport codes. Use as the primary flight dataset for downstream joins, counts, and filters. | Use for: List all flight routes; Filter flights by SourceAirport or DestAirport; Join flights to airline or airport dimensions

accepted.name: flights_with_airline_and_airports
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  f.Airline,
  f.FlightNo,
  f.SourceAirport,
  s.AirportName AS SourceAirport_AirportName,
  s.City AS SourceAirport_City,
  s.Country AS SourceAirport_Country,
  s.CountryAbbrev AS SourceAirport_CountryAbbrev,
  f.DestAirport,
  d.AirportName AS DestAirport_AirportName,
  d.City AS DestAirport_City,
  d.Country AS DestAirport_Country,
  d.CountryAbbrev AS DestAirport_CountryAbbrev,
  a.uid AS uid,
  a.Airline AS Airline_Name,
  a.Abbreviation AS Abbreviation,
  a.Country AS Airline_Country
FROM
  flights AS f
  LEFT JOIN airports AS s ON f.SourceAirport = s.AirportCode
  LEFT JOIN airports AS d ON f.DestAirport = d.AirportCode
  LEFT JOIN airlines AS a ON f.Airline = a.uid
accepted.description: Denormalized flight view joining flights to airline and both source/destination airport dimensions. One row per flight (Airline, FlightNo) with descriptive columns for joins and display. | Use for: Show flights with airline and airport names; Filter flights by source/destination city or airline country; Export denormalized flight records for reporting

accepted.name: flight_counts_by_airline
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  f.Airline AS Airline,
  COUNT(*) AS flight_count
FROM
  flights AS f
GROUP BY
  f.Airline
accepted.description: Aggregate counts of defined flights per airline (carrier). One row per airline uid with the count of distinct FlightNo. Useful for ranking carriers by number of routes or for share calculations. | Use for: How many flights/routes does each airline define?; Compare carrier route breadth; Join counts to airline dimension to show names

accepted.name: outbound_counts_by_airport
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  SourceAirport,
  COUNT(*) AS outbound_flight_count
FROM
  flights
GROUP BY
  SourceAirport
accepted.description: Number of outbound flights (defined routes) per source airport. One row per SourceAirport with count of flights originating there. Useful for identifying busy source airports or for ranking. | Use for: Which airports have the most outgoing routes?; Filter airports by outbound route counts; Join to airports_dim to show city/country for busiest sources

accepted.name: distinct_dest_count_per_source
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  SourceAirport,
  COUNT(DISTINCT DestAirport) AS distinct_dest_count
FROM
  flights
GROUP BY
  SourceAirport
accepted.description: Count of distinct destination airports reachable from each source airport. One row per SourceAirport with a distinct destination count, useful for network connectivity analysis. | Use for: How many unique destinations can you reach from each airport?; Assess airport connectivity or hub status

accepted.name: airline_rank_by_flight_count
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Airline,
  flight_count,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY flight_count DESC) AS airline_flight_rank
FROM
  (SELECT Airline, COUNT(*) AS flight_count FROM flights GROUP BY Airline) AS t
accepted.description: Rank airlines by their number of defined flights (descending). One row per airline with a numeric rank and flight_count. Downstream queries can filter WHERE rank <= K to get top-K carriers. | Use for: Top carriers by number of routes (use WHERE airline_flight_rank <= K); Label carrier tiers by route count rank

accepted.name: airport_outbound_rank
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  SourceAirport,
  outbound_flight_count,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY outbound_flight_count DESC) AS outbound_rank
FROM
  (SELECT SourceAirport, COUNT(*) AS outbound_flight_count FROM flights GROUP BY SourceAirport) AS t
accepted.description: Rank source airports by their outbound flight counts. One row per SourceAirport with outbound_flight_count and rank for easy top-K selection. | Use for: Top source airports by number of outgoing routes (use WHERE outbound_rank <= K); Compare airports by outbound route rank

accepted.name: all_referenced_airports
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT SourceAirport AS AirportCode FROM flights
UNION
SELECT DestAirport AS AirportCode FROM flights
accepted.description: Union of all airports referenced in flights (as sources or destinations). One row per AirportCode present in flights. Useful for restricting airport lists to only those used in flight definitions. | Use for: List all airports that appear in any flight definition; Join to airports_dim to get details for only referenced airports

accepted.name: source_dest_matrix
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  SourceAirport,
  DestAirport,
  COUNT(*) AS route_count
FROM
  flights
GROUP BY
  SourceAirport,
  DestAirport
accepted.description: Wide reshaped view counting defined routes from each source airport to each destination airport. One row per SourceAirport with columns for each DestAirport encoded as (Dest_<AirportCode> = count). Useful for pivot-style network matrices. NOTE: downstream queries may need to aggregate or filter the matrix; this CTE produces a long-form pivot-ready aggregation (source/dest/count) which can be pivoted further in the client. | Use for: Build a matrix of routes between airports; Show counts of routes between specific source-destination pairs

accepted.name: flights_with_airport_countries
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  f.Airline,
  f.FlightNo,
  f.SourceAirport,
  s.Country AS SourceAirport_Country,
  f.DestAirport,
  d.Country AS DestAirport_Country
FROM
  flights AS f
  LEFT JOIN airports AS s ON f.SourceAirport = s.AirportCode
  LEFT JOIN airports AS d ON f.DestAirport = d.AirportCode
accepted.description: Flights augmented with source and destination airport country and airline id—useful for country-level network analysis or filtering flights that cross countries. | Use for: Identify international vs domestic routes by comparing SourceAirport_Country and DestAirport_Country; Filter flights by source or dest country
